summary.tagline: Lough Derg, historically Lough Dergart (Irish: Loch Deirgeirt), is a freshwater lake in the Shannon River Basi

days.title: North and East Shores
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Portumna
stops.detail: The Shannon's inflow is located at Portumna, while its outflow is at Killaloe.

stops.name: Dromineer
stops.detail: On the eastern shore, near the village of Dromineer, the River Nenagh flows into the lake.

stops.name: Illaunmore
stops.detail: The largest island, measuring 0.61 km², is called Illaunmore.

days.title: South and West Bays
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Scariff–Youghal–Bay
stops.detail: The lough measures its greatest width of 13 km with its southern foothills in the Scariff-Youghal Bay section.

stops.name: Parkers Point
stops.detail: The deepest point is at Parkers Point; there, a small trench drops down to 36 m.

stops.name: Holy Island
stops.detail: The most famous is Holy Island, Irish Inis Cealtra; on it stand the ruins of an abbey from the 7th century, a bullaun, and a round tower.
